l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The text introduces RAGAS (Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment), a framework for evaluating Retrieval Augmented Generation pipelines without reference annotations. It concerns RAG systems, which combine a retrieval module with an LLM-based generation module and provide large language models with knowledge from a reference corpus. RAGAS evaluates retrieval quality, the faithful use of retrieved passages, and the quality of generated responses through a suite of reference-free metrics. The framework is intended to support faster evaluation cycles for RAG architectures.

l: RAGAS, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: RAGAS, or Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment, is introduced as a framework for reference-free evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation pipelines. It provides metrics for assessing retrieval, faithful use of retrieved context, and generation quality.

l: RAG systems, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: RAG systems are composed of a retrieval module and an LLM-based generation module. They provide large language models with knowledge from a reference corpus, which can help keep systems up to date and reduce the risk of hallucinations.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Large language models receive knowledge from a reference corpus through RAG systems. This access can help keep LLM-based systems up to date and reduce the risk of hallucinations.

l: reference corpus, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: A reference corpus supplies knowledge to large language models through RAG systems. The text presents this knowledge as a way to support up-to-date systems and reduce hallucinations.

l: end-to-end evaluation framework for RAG, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: RAG evaluation is challenging because it must consider retrieval quality, the ability of an LLM to use retrieved passages faithfully, and the quality of the generation itself. RAGAS is proposed to enable this evaluation without ground-truth human annotations.

l: retrieval quality, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Retrieval quality concerns the ability of a retrieval system to identify relevant and focused context passages. RAGAS includes metrics intended to assess this dimension.

l: generation quality, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: Generation quality is one of the dimensions that must be considered when evaluating RAG architectures. RAGAS includes metrics for assessing the quality of the generated response.

l: metrics, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: RAGAS puts forward a suite of metrics for evaluating different dimensions of RAG architectures without relying on ground-truth human annotations. The metrics are intended to support faster evaluation cycles.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: The text explains that language models struggle with post-training events and knowledge that is rarely mentioned in their training corpus. Retrieval Augmented Generation addresses these issues by retrieving relevant passages and providing them to a language model with the original question. Evaluating RAG systems requires tuning and is often difficult because perplexity may not predict downstream performance and closed models may not expose probabilities. The paper presents RAGAS, a framework for automatically assessing retrieval-augmented generation systems without requiring reference answers.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Language models can struggle to answer questions about events that occurred after training and to memorize knowledge that is rarely mentioned in the training corpus. Standard language models can use retrieved documents added to their input, including when they are available only through APIs.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Retrieval Augmented Generation addresses limitations of language models by retrieving relevant passages from a corpus and providing them, together with the original question, to the language model. Its performance depends on factors including the retrieval model, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation.

l: reference corpus, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: A corpus supplies passages that can be retrieved and given to a language model as part of Retrieval Augmented Generation. Perplexity-based evaluation may measure performance on a reference corpus, but this is not always predictive of downstream performance.

l: retrieved context, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Retrieved passages are selected from a corpus and fed to the language model along with the original question. Their usefulness is one of the aspects that automated evaluation of retrieval-augmented systems seeks to assess.

l: question answering, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Question answering is a common task for evaluating retrieval-augmented systems. Existing evaluations usually focus on datasets with short extractive answers, which may not represent how a system will be used.

l: prompt, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Prompt formulation is one of the factors that can affect the overall performance of a retrieval-augmented system. It therefore requires tuning alongside the retrieval model, corpus, and language model.

l: RAG systems, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: A RAG system is affected by its retrieval model, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation. It can be evaluated through measures such as perplexity or question answering, although these approaches have limitations.

l: RAGAS, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: RAGAS is a framework for the automated assessment of retrieval augmented generation systems. It focuses on settings where reference answers may be unavailable and estimates proxies for correctness as well as the usefulness of retrieved passages. RAGAS integrates with llama-index and Langchain so developers can use it within standard RAG workflows.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: This unit reviews methods for estimating the faithfulness and factuality of LLM-generated responses, including prompting, token probabilities, hidden states, and sampling multiple answers. It describes BARTScore, Kadavath et al.'s multiple-choice approach, Azaria and Mitchell's hidden-state classifier, and SelfCheckGPT. It also surveys LLM-based evaluation of fluency and other text-generation qualities, including direct scoring and candidate selection. Finally, it discusses reference-based metrics such as BERTScore, MoverScore, and BARTScore.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: LLMs are studied for detecting hallucinations and estimating the factuality or faithfulness of generated responses. They are also used to evaluate qualities of generated text, although their judgments can be sensitive to prompt design and answer order.

l: hallucination detection, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: Hallucination detection in LLM-generated responses has been extensively studied. Existing models can struggle with hallucination detection when standard prompting strategies are used.

l: faithfulness estimation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: Faithfulness estimation methods include few-shot prompting, linking responses to external knowledge bases, analyzing token probabilities, training classifiers on hidden states, and sampling multiple answers. Some of these methods are unsuitable when systems do not expose hidden states or token probabilities.

l: text generation evaluation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: LLMs are used to automatically evaluate aspects of generated text beyond factuality, including fluency and overall answer quality. Evaluation can involve scoring individual answers or selecting the best answer from several candidates.

l: BARTScore, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: BARTScore estimates factuality using the conditional probability of generated text given the input. It can also use reference answers to estimate precision and recall through conditional generation probabilities.

l: SelfCheckGPT, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: SelfCheckGPT samples multiple answers to assess factuality without relying on token probabilities. It is based on the expectation that factual answers are more semantically stable across samples than hallucinated answers.

l: ChatGPT, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: ChatGPT does not provide access to token probabilities, so methods such as sampling multiple answers are needed to assess its outputs. It can also be directly asked to evaluate an answer using a numerical or star-based rating.

l: GPT-4, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: GPT-4 does not provide access to token probabilities, requiring alternative evaluation methods. These methods include sampling multiple answers or directly asking the model to assess a particular aspect of an answer.

l: reference answers, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: Reference answers are commonly used to evaluate text-generation systems. BERTScore, MoverScore, and BARTScore compare or condition on reference answers to estimate similarity, precision, or recall.

l: answer, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: Generated answers are evaluated for factuality, fluency, and other qualities. Their stability across samples can indicate factuality, while their similarity to reference answers can support automated evaluation.

l: prompting strategies, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 2 / Estimating faithfulness using LLMs .. Automated evaluation of text generation systems
s: Few-shot and standard prompting strategies have been used to predict factuality and evaluate generated text. Existing models may struggle to detect hallucinations with standard prompting, and evaluation results can be sensitive to prompt design.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: The unit describes evaluation strategies for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems without human-annotated datasets or reference answers. It identifies faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance as central quality aspects, with faithfulness concerning whether a generated answer is grounded in the retrieved context. It explains that large language models can be prompted to measure these aspects automatically, using gpt-3.5-turbo-16k in the reported implementation and experiments. For faithfulness, the system first extracts focused statements from each sentence of the generated answer so they can be checked against the context.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: RAG systems retrieve context for a question and use that context to generate an answer. They are evaluated using reference-free metrics because human-annotated datasets or reference answers are usually unavailable.

l: question, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: The question is used to retrieve context and is provided with the answer when an LLM extracts statements from that answer.

l: retrieved context, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: The retrieved context is intended to ground and justify the generated answer. Its relevance is also evaluated based on whether it is focused and contains little irrelevant information.

l: answer, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: The generated answer should address the question and remain grounded in the retrieved context. For faithfulness evaluation, it is decomposed into shorter, focused statements.

l: faithfulness, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: Faithfulness concerns whether claims in the answer can be inferred from the given context. It helps reduce hallucinations and supports the use of retrieved sources as justifications.

l: answer relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: Answer relevance concerns whether the generated answer addresses the actual question that was provided.

l: context relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: Context relevance concerns whether the retrieved context is focused and contains as little irrelevant information as possible. Long or unfocused passages can increase costs and make it harder for LLMs to use information, especially information in the middle of a passage.

l: metrics, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: The evaluation metrics are fully self-contained and reference-free. They target faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance and can be measured by prompting an LLM.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: A large language model is prompted to evaluate the three quality aspects. In the implementation and experiments described, prompts were evaluated using the gpt-3.5-turbo-16k model available through the OpenAI API.

l: statements, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 3 .. Faithfulness
s: Statements are extracted from the generated answer by creating one or more statements from each sentence. Their purpose is to decompose longer sentences into shorter and more focused assertions for faithfulness evaluation.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The unit describes how an LLM evaluates whether statements in an answer can be inferred from a question's context using a verification function. It defines the faithfulness score as the proportion of supported statements and explains how answer relevance is estimated by generating questions from an answer and comparing their embeddings with the original question. It also defines context relevance as the proportion of context sentences extracted as necessary for answering the question. The procedures use specified prompts and, for answer relevance, the text-embedding-ada-002 model and cosine similarity.

l: faithfulness, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The faithfulness score, F, is computed as the number of supported statements divided by the total number of statements in the answer.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The LLM determines whether each statement can be inferred from the context and provides a brief explanation followed by a Yes/No verdict. It also generates potential questions from an answer and extracts context sentences relevant to a question.

l: statements, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: A statement is evaluated for whether the information in the context supports it. The verification prompt requires an explanation and a final Yes/No verdict for each statement.

l: retrieved context, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The context is used to verify statements and is assessed for whether it contains only information needed to answer the question. Relevant sentences are extracted from it without modification.

l: question, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The question is compared with questions generated from the answer to estimate answer relevance. It is also used to identify which context sentences are needed to answer it.

l: answer, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: The answer is evaluated for faithfulness and relevance. Potential questions are generated from it, and their embedding similarities to the original question contribute to the answer relevance score.

l: answer relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: Answer relevance measures how directly an answer addresses the question, penalizing incompleteness and redundant information without considering factuality. It is calculated as the average cosine similarity between the original question and questions generated from the answer.

l: context relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening .. Context relevance
s: Context relevance measures the extent to which the context contains only information needed to answer the question. It is calculated as the number of extracted relevant sentences divided by the total number of sentences in the context.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The WikiEval Dataset was created to evaluate the proposed framework using question-context-answer triples with human judgments. The dataset is intended to assess faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance, and to compare these judgments with the framework’s metrics. Its creators selected 50 Wikipedia pages about events since the start of 2022, prioritizing pages with recent edits. ChatGPT was then asked to formulate questions answerable from each page’s introductory section.

l: WikiEval, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The WikiEval Dataset was created to provide question-context-answer triples annotated with human judgments. It contains material based on 50 Wikipedia pages covering events since the start of 2022.

l: end-to-end evaluation framework for RAG, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The proposed framework is evaluated using the WikiEval Dataset. Its metrics are compared with human assessments of faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance.

l: human judgements, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Human judgments are used to annotate question-context-answer triples for faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance.

l: metrics, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The metrics are evaluated by comparing their assessments with human judgments of faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance.

l: Wikipedia, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: Wikipedia provides the pages used to construct the WikiEval Dataset. The selected pages cover events that have happened since the start of 2022.

l: 50 Wikipedia pages, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: The 50 Wikipedia pages were selected for the WikiEval Dataset, with priority given to pages with recent edits. Each page covers an event since the start of 2022.

l: ChatGPT, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 4
s: ChatGPT was asked to suggest a question for each selected page. The question had to be answerable from the page’s introductory section and fully answered by the given context.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: The unit describes quality guidelines for generating questions and evaluates answers in the WikiEval dataset. ChatGPT was used to answer questions with and without context and to generate candidate answers with lower answer relevance. Human annotators assessed faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance, achieving about 95% agreement for faithfulness and context relevance and about 90% for answer relevance. The unit presents examples involving the film Oppenheimer and the PSLV-C56 mission.

l: WikiEval, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: The WikiEval dataset contains examples used to assess faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. Its examples include questions about Oppenheimer and the PSLV-C56 mission, with answers demonstrating high and low quality.

l: ChatGPT, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: ChatGPT was used to answer generated questions with their introductory sections as context and to answer questions without additional context. It was also used to generate candidate answers with lower answer relevance and, in some cases, to complete contexts when Wikipedia pages lacked back-links.

l: human annotators, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Two fluent-English human annotators judged faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. They agreed in around 95% of cases for faithfulness and context relevance and around 90% of cases for answer relevance, resolving disagreements through discussion.

l: faithfulness, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Faithfulness was evaluated by comparing a standard ChatGPT answer with an answer generated without additional context, using the question and corresponding Wikipedia page. The unit illustrates high faithfulness with the correct identification of Christopher Nolan and Cillian Murphy and low faithfulness with incorrect names.

l: answer relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Answer relevance was evaluated by comparing a complete answer with an incomplete answer. The high-relevance example gives the PSLV-C56 launch date, time, and location, while the low-relevance example omits the requested launch details and gives unrelated information.

l: context relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: Context relevance was measured by adding related but less relevant sentences to the original context through back-links to the corresponding Wikipedia page. For pages without back-links, ChatGPT was used to complete the context.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: The Experiments section evaluates RAGAS metrics against human assessments from the WikiEval dataset using pairwise comparisons of faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. RAGAS agrees more closely with human annotators than the GPT Score and GPT Ranking baselines, while context relevance is identified as the hardest dimension to evaluate. The reproducibility analysis finds that JSON-formatted outputs make RAGAS scores more consistent across successive runs. The unit also discusses challenges caused by randomness, undocumented API changes, and structured-output requirements when using large language models.

l: current set of experiments, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Experiments compare RAGAS with GPT Score and GPT Ranking on agreement with human assessments in WikiEval. They also examine the reproducibility of RAGAS scores with and without JSON formatting.

l: RAGAS, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: RAGAS evaluates faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. Its predictions are more closely aligned with human annotators than the two baselines, and its scores are more consistent when outputs are JSON formatted.

l: WikiEval, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: WikiEval contains instances in which a model compares two answers or two context fragments. The experiments measure how often the model’s preferred candidate matches the preference of human annotators.

l: human annotators, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Human annotators provide the preferences used to assess model agreement in WikiEval. Their judgments serve as the reference for accuracy comparisons.

l: faithfulness, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Faithfulness measures the consistency of an answer with its given context and penalizes claims that cannot be deduced from that context. RAGAS achieves high agreement with human judgments on this dimension.

l: answer relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Answer relevance measures whether a response directly addresses and appropriately answers a question, while penalizing redundancy or incompleteness. Agreement is lower on this dimension because candidate answers often differ only subtly.

l: context relevancy, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Context relevance evaluates whether context is relevant to the question and identifies crucial information. It is the hardest quality dimension to evaluate, particularly for longer contexts.

l: GPT Score, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: GPT Score asks ChatGPT to assign each candidate a score from 0 to 10 for faithfulness, answer relevance, or context relevance. Ties are broken randomly, and its agreement with human annotators is lower than RAGAS’s.

l: GPT Ranking, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: GPT Ranking asks ChatGPT to select the preferred answer or context based on a definition of the relevant quality metric. Its agreement with human annotators is lower than that of RAGAS.

l: ChatGPT, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: ChatGPT is used in the GPT Score and GPT Ranking baselines. It often struggles to select the crucial sentences from contexts, especially when the contexts are long.

l: LLMs, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Large language models can produce different results across runs because of undocumented API changes or inherent neural-network randomness. Experiments therefore require attention to reliable software, reproducibility, and structured JSON output.

l: JSON, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: JSON formatting is required for structured outputs from the language model. RAGAS scores are more consistent across successive runs when JSON formatting is used than when it is not.

l: reproducibility, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 5 .. 5.1
s: Reproducibility is challenging when experiments use large language models because repeated runs may produce different results. The unit evaluates reproducibility by comparing RAGAS scores across runs with and without JSON formatting.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 6
s: RAGAS provides access to metrics and datasets through an easy-to-use Python API. The unit shows how to load the Amnesty QA dataset, evaluate its evaluation split with faithfulness, answer relevancy, and context relevancy metrics, and export the results to a pandas dataframe. The metrics available at ragas.metrics use OpenAI's API by default, although other LLMs can also be used for evaluation.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, 7
s: The unit concludes that automated reference-free evaluation is needed for RAG systems. It proposes an evaluation framework covering faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. It introduces WikiEval, a dataset containing human judgements of these aspects, and describes RAGAS, an implementation of them. Evaluation on WikiEval found that RAGAS predictions closely aligned with human judgments, especially for faithfulness and answer relevance.

l: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation, opening
s: RAGAS relies heavily on the performance of LLMs to evaluate different components. The experiments show that its metrics have a high correlation with human judgements, but LLM limitations remain a concern. The text calls for careful review of LLM suitability, ideally prioritizing open models over paid APIs, for RAGAS and related contributions. RAGAS will continue encouraging fair systems built on top of it as more users gain access to accurate RAG systems.

l: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: The abstract concerns the evaluation and optimization of retrieval-augmented generation for medical question answering. It introduces the Medical Information Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation (MIRAGE), a benchmark with 7,663 questions from five medical QA datasets, and the MEDRAG toolkit. Experiments evaluated 41 combinations of medical corpora, retrievers, and backbone LLMs using over 1.8 trillion prompt tokens. MEDRAG improved six LLMs by up to 18% over chain-of-thought prompting, while the study also identified log-linear scaling and “lost-in-the-middle” effects in medical RAG.

s: Large language models have achieved state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of medical question answering tasks, but they still face challenges from hallucinations and outdated knowledge.

s: Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a promising solution to hallucinations and outdated knowledge in large language models and has been widely adopted.

l: MEDRAG, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: MEDRAG is introduced as a toolkit for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems. Using MEDRAG, the study ran large-scale experiments across 41 combinations of corpora, retrievers, and backbone LLMs, and found accuracy improvements of up to 18% over chain-of-thought prompting for six LLMs.

l: document collections, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Medical corpora were evaluated in combination with retrievers and backbone LLMs. The results indicate that combining various medical corpora and retrievers achieves the best performance.

l: retrievers, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Retrievers were evaluated as components of medical retrieval-augmented generation systems. The best performance was achieved when various retrievers were combined with various medical corpora.

l: backbone LLMs, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Backbone LLMs were included in 41 evaluated combinations with different corpora and retrievers. MEDRAG improved the accuracy of six different LLMs by up to 18% over chain-of-thought prompting.

l: chain-of-thought prompting, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Chain-of-thought prompting served as a baseline for comparison. MEDRAG improved the accuracy of six different LLMs by up to 18% over this baseline.

l: GPT-3.5, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: GPT-3.5 reached GPT-4-level performance when using MEDRAG, according to the abstract.

l: Mixtral, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Mixtral reached GPT-4-level performance when using MEDRAG, according to the abstract.

l: GPT-4, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: GPT-4-level performance was reached by GPT-3.5 and Mixtral with MEDRAG.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: Medical RAG was found to exhibit a log-linear scaling property and “lost-in-the-middle” effects.

l: medical information retrieval-augmented generation evaluation experiments, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Abstract
s: The medical information retrieval-augmented generation evaluation experiments used over 1.8 trillion prompt tokens to test 41 combinations of different corpora, retrievers, and backbone LLMs.

l: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: The unit concerns Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and their use in biomedical and medical question answering. It introduces MIRAGE, a benchmark with 7,663 questions from five biomedical QA datasets, and MEDRAG, a toolkit covering five corpora, four retrievers, and six LLMs. The evaluation finds that MEDRAG improves performance over chain-of-thought prompting, that corpus and retriever preferences vary by task, and that combining corpora or retrievers can be beneficial. The unit also reports log-linear scaling with the number of retrieved snippets and a “lost-in-the-middle” effect based on the position of the ground-truth snippet.

l: Large Language Models, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Large Language Models have transformed online information seeking and show strong question-answering capabilities in general and medical domains. They can nevertheless produce plausible but factually incorrect responses and may lack recent knowledge, such as updated clinical guidelines.

l: medical question answering, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Question answering is presented as a capability of Large Language Models in both general and medical domains. The MIRAGE benchmark evaluates medical question answering in zero-shot settings.

l: hallucination, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Hallucination refers to the generation of plausible-sounding but factually incorrect responses by Large Language Models. The unit identifies it as a major concern for medical applications.

l: healthcare, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Healthcare is described as a high-stakes domain in which outdated knowledge and hallucinated responses from Large Language Models can be especially dangerous.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation provides Large Language Models with relevant documents from up-to-date and trustworthy collections. It can reduce the effects of hallucination and outdated knowledge while improving transparency by grounding reasoning in retrieved documents.

l: RAG systems in medicine, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Medical RAG systems contain flexible components including document collections, retrieval algorithms, and backbone Large Language Models. The unit studies how these components affect performance and provides practical recommendations for biomedical applications.

l: MIRAGE, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: MIRAGE is introduced as a benchmark for systematically comparing medical RAG systems. It contains 7,663 questions from five biomedical QA datasets and evaluates zero-shot RAG with question-only retrieval.

l: Medical Information Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Medical Information Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation is the expansion of MIRAGE. It names the benchmark designed to evaluate different components and configurations of medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.

l: MEDRAG, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: MEDRAG is an easy-to-use medical RAG toolkit covering five corpora, four retrievers, and six general or domain-specific Large Language Models. Its configurations improve performance on MIRAGE relative to chain-of-thought prompting, with relative gains of 1% to 18% across different models.

l: biomedical question answering, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Medical question answering is the application area evaluated by MIRAGE and supported by MEDRAG. The benchmark focuses on zero-shot performance and uses only the question, rather than answer options, during retrieval.

l: retrievers, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: Retrievers are one of the configurable components of medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. On MIRAGE, BM25 and MedCPT perform strongly, and combining multiple retrievers can further improve performance.

l: BM25, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: BM25 is a retriever evaluated in MEDRAG. It displays superior performance on the MIRAGE benchmark, alongside the domain-specific MedCPT retriever.

l: MedCPT, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: MedCPT is a domain-specific retriever evaluated in MEDRAG. It displays superior performance on MIRAGE, and performance can be further enhanced by combining it with other retrievers.

l: PubMed, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Introduction
s: PubMed is evaluated as one of the retrieval corpora in MEDRAG. It is described as a robust choice across all MIRAGE tasks, whereas point-of-care articles and textbooks are mainly helpful for examination questions.

l: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: The unit reviews Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), biomedical question answering, and related evaluation settings. Lewis et al. (2020) proposed RAG to improve knowledge-intensive generation by incorporating retrieved information, and later studies developed improvements and biomedical applications. The text states that systematic biomedical evaluations have generally focused on vanilla large language models without RAG, while this study provides the first systematic evaluation of RAG systems in medicine. It also explains that large language models have surpassed BERT-based models on medical question answering and that the study evaluates RAG using medical QA datasets and both RAG and question-only retrieval settings.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: Lewis et al. (2020) proposed Retrieval-Augmented Generation to enhance generation on knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating retrieved relevant information. It can ground large language models in provided contexts, mitigate hallucinations, and supply up-to-date knowledge that may not be encoded by the models.

l: biomedical question answering, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: Biomedical question answering is a widely studied task because information needs in biomedicine are often expressed as natural language questions. The unit describes medical QA datasets as tools for evaluating biomedical capabilities and for testing whether RAG systems retrieve and use relevant contexts.

l: Large Language Models, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: Large language models have outperformed BERT-based models by large margins on medical question answering. Biomedical QA datasets are used to evaluate both general and domain-specific large language models.

l: BERT, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: BERT-based models were previously state-of-the-art methods for medical question answering. They have been outperformed by large language models by large margins.

l: RAG systems in medicine, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: RAG systems in medicine have been explored for literature information-seeking and clinical decision-making. The unit states that prior evaluations were not comprehensive and presents this study as the first systematic evaluation of RAG systems in medicine.

l: medical QA datasets, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: Medical QA datasets are commonly used to evaluate the biomedical capabilities of general and domain-specific large language models. In this study, they are used to test whether a RAG system can retrieve and leverage relevant contexts.

l: Question-Only Retrieval, Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine, Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Generation .. Biomedical Question Answering
s: Question-only retrieval is included alongside RAG in the study's evaluation settings. The text describes this combination as a more realistic evaluation for medical question answering.
